contradictions.claim_a: Any React setState or rerender is a design failure that Entity Management was engineered to eliminate.
contradictions.claim_b: Entity Management 3.0.2 itself uses React state for isolated CRUD buffers and mutation status, and its hooks subscribe to Zustand.
contradictions.resolution: Reject the absolute claim. The valid invariant is that business state has one explicit authority and subscriptions are narrow; necessary UI reconciliation remains.

contradictions.claim_a: upsertEntities avoids N separate writes during list hydration.
contradictions.claim_b: useEntities follows the batch upsert with N setEntityFetched writes.
contradictions.resolution: The data slice is batched, but the complete list-ingestion operation is not. Treat this as an upstream defect and add one atomic fetched-list action.

contradictions.claim_a: The Session Configuration panel persists model and context overrides.
contradictions.claim_b: Its JSON field names do not match the backend contract, it never reads persisted session state, and the turn builder uses the agent model.
contradictions.resolution: Classify the panel as a dead facade until an installed-browser inference run proves the saved session model changes effective routing.

contradictions.claim_a: Switching from per-row upsertEntity to useEntities 3.0.2 is sufficient to eliminate the freeze class.
contradictions.claim_b: useEntities 3.0.2 still has unbounded N lifecycle publications.
contradictions.resolution: Fix and release the upstream atomic-ingestion primitive first, then migrate UAR to the transport/domain-hook path and the configured subset.
